Content: Screenshot
I didn't expect there to be a place like this beneath Rabelle College.
Before Sundermere base was built, this was a research facility for Augmented Resonance Effects and Void Storm countermeasures. It's been decommissioned for years.
The Executive Committee told me I could do whatever I wanted with the space. So I used my Forte to do some light remodeling.
Memories of my students that should exist only in my mind, here... they become real. A tangible piece to display.
You're using your Forte to do all this? How long did it take you to create this?
However long it took, it was worth it... So the ones who "stay" don't just stay, and the ones who "leave" don't just leave.
We still have some time. If you're interested, feel free to look around.
The exhibits we're looking for are here.
Hmm? Behind the wall?
Don't forget, this is my Memory Palace. Naturally, memory locks require memory keys to unlock.
Allow me to demonstrate—This fancy trick only works in this little domain of mine.
This is the very reason I built this exhibition hall in the first place.
What is it?
Professor, do you trust me?
Lucilla?
You spaced out there. Are you alright?
I'm fine. Just had a dream that only lasted a few seconds. Rather fascinating.
Maybe it's a good idea to rest before the review starts?
Don't worry. I promise you I'll crash the second this is over. But right now, we must bring these exhibits with us.
Will a few exhibits be enough to sway them?
(She usually knows exactly how to sell anything, so why does she look so hesitant now?)
Thank you for your trust. I know you have a thousand questions burning in your mind.
"How will she handle the New Fed?" "What's her plan for the Synchronists with the Exostrider gone?" Forgive me for not having the answers just yet.
I know you'd never harm the students. That's the only answer I need.
I... Terrible timing for a compliment, {PlayerName}.
Anyway. Let's take these two exhibits and—
See you soon, Professor.
Some kind of force pulled us down here. Do you know where we are?
If my memory serves, we're directly beneath the exhibition hall.
This way.
A Synchronist's cockpit? Was this the prototype?
It looks the part, but this was actually our "Plan B." Designed without safety limiters to get sync rates up quick. Lets a Synchronist pilot the Exostrider by force.
I know, I know. It was meant as a last resort if civilization was staring down extinction. The project was terminated after the initial trials.
The Synchronists who volunteered... In the end, they lost their ability to resonate with the Exostrider ever again.
What our students are facing now isn't new.
I just hope I can do better by them this time.
What's happening?
Something rather unpleasant, I imagine.
Lucilla...
Fine, no more jokes. Honestly, anyone watching would think you're the one facing the board. There, there, I know the way out.
Remember what I told you before entering the Dark Side? About the memories I erase periodically that can never be recovered?
Some things... I can't bear to remember, but I also can't bear to forget, so I store them here. Looks like some of them are tired of being locked up...
{PlayerName}, look up. The exit is right above. We can use this <ano=Photo>key</ano> to leave. But I need your help to get there.
Everything here is from my memory, but I know you are real. And wherever you are, that must be reality.
I understand. I'll be your reference point. But what about that girl? Are we just leaving her?
{PlayerName}, do you have any experience dealing with children? Tell me, what makes a child the most flustered when they're playing hide-and-seek?
...Ah. I see.
Now, come along. Let's treat this little escape as a warm-up for the review.
Welcome to the Anti-Voidmatter Materials Lab. It's where they first developed the materials for the Academy's Antivoid Canopy.
What's all of that in the center of the room?
The scrap of the day. Even the best recycling can only keep up with so much.
Let's look around to see if there are any leads.
Only one in a thousand makes the cut. Which means nine hundred ninety-nine don't.
People see the Antivoid Canopy and praise its ingenuity. They'll never get to see the blueprints of the ones who were rejected.
Is this artificial Retroact Rain?
Oh, dear me. This is but a pale imitation.

Among the Synchronists who survived the experiments, there was one from Jinzhou. Once he realized he'd never resonate with the Exostrider, he returned home and joined the Ministry of Development's Defense Division.
There, he and his colleagues worked together to develop Jinzhou's Retroact Rain defenses.
You're saying the shields against Retroact Rain and Void Storms share the same origin?
Not exactly. His approach didn't work on Void Storms at all... and it was discarded. Long ago.
Before he left the Academy, the only things he asked to take with him were a few sheets of material buried under that pile of junk.
I often wonder... was he just reluctant to let go of his design? Or had he already mapped out how to protect his hometown?
The girl who trapped us here... She must be trying to show us something through this memory.
Hmm. Seems I've been getting schooled by my own students a lot lately...
Let's go. It's time to move on to the next "classroom."
Well... we made quite the headway there, didn't we?
That said, I'm glad to see we're at least moving.
Let's keep heading upwards. We'll find our way out soon enough.
What's wrong?
Stay where I can see you, {PlayerName}. We've wandered into an unpleasant memory.
It's far too easy to get lost in here...
It doesn't look like there's a way to cross the barrier ahead.
Hmm... I have an idea.
{PlayerName}, just go with me on this, alright?
Clear as day, Madam. Your daughter isn't sick. She has awakened her Forte, and it's a remarkably rare memory-type.
Congratulations! I'm certain she'll make an immense contribution to the New Federation one day.
Nonsense! My Luci will never become a Resonator!
Mom...
I don't want to be a Resonator. Please... no!
Luci!
Lucilla?
(Without a "reference point", she's getting pulled into the deep end of her memories. I need to find her before too much time passes.)
Not good.
Are you still there, Lucilla?
Yes.
Then why aren't you answering?
What do you want me to say?
You can say "Okay," or "I understand."
This is the perfect moment—while our opponents are spread too thin, we take the reins. Just like the time you became President...
Don't worry about the narrative. We'll play the villain. You just act tough, rope the independent auditor in, and we'll force another round of review.
You fight hard. We express our "concerns." And then... we both take a step back. As long as we ensure our control over the future of the Synchronist Program, nothing else matters.
And what do you want from my students?
Simple. We both get what we want. They have talent, and we help them achieve their dreams. And it'll be their choice.
Their choice? Whose dreams are we really achieving?
It will be their choice, Lucilla. My Luci. I won't speak of your past choices, but tell me, has there been a single choice that wasn't your own?
I still refuse.
There. Just like that. "Act tough," "fight hard," and then we both "take a step back" at the review...
From the Academy to the Pioneer Association, then to the Spacetrek Collective, and now here… No wonder I was never cut out to be President.
Watch out! That's "me" from the Dark Side. I used this memory to trap her.
When are you going to tell {Male=him;Female=her}, Professor Lucilla? President Lucilla? That you've already made a deal with the New Federation?
Let's go.
You think you can outrun yourself, Lucilla?
(I need to know the truth.)
(I trust Lucilla. That's enough.)
Your plan... Are you just following the New Federation's playbook?
Don't let her get to you. How could I ever sell out my students? I have a plan, it's just...
Before the meeting starts, I need you to take the time to fill me in on what's really happening.
Thank you. I promise, I'd never let the New Federation lay a single finger on my students. But...
That's just her wishful thinking. A moth to the flame, daring the sky with wings of wax.
Your students will die because of you!
...Let's leave this place, {PlayerName}.
Is this it? This is as far as we've got?
That just means we'd better pick up the pace.

Once again, I found the courage to step into this room. Time flows here, silent and peaceful, and the Academy is alive and thriving. We've come so much further than I ever dreamed. I wish you were here to see it.
Is that Sundermere? Are we back before the Starward Riseway was even built?
Most of the students who lost their Synchronist status in those forced sync trials decided to return home. All but one.
She told me it wasn't that she'd lost the Exostrider. The Exostrider had lost her.
She said she'd designed a revolutionary transport method.  A "rocket piercing the sky." A way to bridge that "sky" and the "earth."
This was the day she tested it. Her first crewed flight.
Then that wasn't a falling star. It was—
A spacecraft. Carrying the most brilliant student I've ever known.
Amiya to Sundermere Lookout. Professor, can you hear me?!
Yes.
The weather couldn't be more perfect today! Oh, and I just saw a super huge Soliskin! I'll snap a picture for you as soon as I can!
Okay.
Professor? You don't sound like your usual self. Are those investors giving you a hard time again?
No, it's not that. I just... I haven't slept much lately. I'm a little tired. That's all.
...Professor, do you trust us?
Hey, remember that old Huanglong saying? "Know the way at dawn, and... and something-something at dusk?" Ugh, it went right out of my head!
I can't remember it either...
That's okay! I'll look it up and tell you the second the experiment is over!
Talk to you soon!
Please, {PlayerName}...
From the way it fell, Voidmatter must've pierced the shielding mid-flight. But if we'd reinforced the coating... Hmm...
What kind of civilization do you think built the Exostrider? If they were that advanced... do you think they'd already defeated the Threnodians? Overcome the Lament?
But before they reached the stars, they must have fallen too. Again and again.
Go. Be our eyes. Walk with humanity.
Please give this to our teacher. Humanity's smallest step... and everything we had to give.
This isn't good.
Lucilla!
Lucilla, your emotions are affecting this domain! It's dangerous!
Staying here is the real danger. We have to leave.
Almost there.
As long as we keep moving upward, we'll find the way out.
So this is why you wouldn't tell me what your plan was.
This "way out" you've been building for the Synchronists... It's just a dead end, isn't it?
I don't want the New Federation to lay their dirty hands on my students. But the more I think about it rationally, the more I realize I can't reject their offer.
Because on what grounds can I propose a plan that might kill them?
I think I know why that girl trapped you here.
What?
You're terrified that your proposal will be their end.
You're afraid because you know they'll support any plan you bring to the table.
Because you're their teacher.
Because no one in this world understands them the way you do.
Another lesson from my own student, huh...
See you later, {PlayerName}.
I hope humanity can soar even higher!
I hope humanity can venture even farther!
I hope humanity can weather any storm!
Professor, what's your dream?
My dream? My dream is simply to see all of yours come true.
See you later, Professor.
Let's go. Together this time.
Professor, can you hear me?!
I hear you. Loud and clear.
The weather couldn't be more perfect today! Oh, and I just saw a super huge Soliskin!
Yes, I see it too. You're right, it's absolutely huge.
Great! I thought you weren't gonna believe me!
Right, I'll see you soon!
Mm, see you soon!
The accident report is indisputable. "Cable insulation failure leading to flight control abnormality." But the truth is simpler. I approved the plan. I killed her.

I wrestled with it for so long. What's a teacher supposed to do when a student dreams something so brilliantly insane? But she chose the sky. And I thought... at least let her have one chance to fall.
Are you hanging in there alright?
I could ask you the same.
Let's regroup ASAP.
Agreed. The space here seems to be constantly shifting. We'll need to rendezvous in a memory vivid enough for me. Keep this photo I'm sending over.
Find a suitable place. You know what to do... And keep your wits about you, Rover. Don't get yourself lost in a memory.
Emergency mode engaged. Please enter key.
LlO0i1l
LI0Oi1l
LI0Oil1
Time to do it my way!
Incorrect Password!
Access Granted!
Incorrect Password!
There should be a console around. Follow my instructions to disable the security system.
First, initiate emergency mode. Type in: LI0Oi1l. Then select Lift Restrictions, and you're good to go.
Heh... Has anyone ever told you that you're not the most photogenic?
They have now.
No more teasing. This shot will have to suffice...
You could've erased this memory. Why keep something so dangerous locked away?
To keep the sting fresh. A sharp reminder of the cost of slipping up if I ever get too comfortable in the Academy's peace.
*Yawn*
Should we pick up the pace a little?
Where was this enthusiasm during class, hmm?
Do you want to stop and take a rest?
Not even close.
Do you want to stop and take a rest?
Not even close.
Lucilla, wait!
I'll have to pay for any property damage out of my own pocket, you know...
So please, try to be gentle with the facilities.
There's probably a device nearby controlling the barrier.
Let it go, Lucilla. Face what you know is reality...
That staircase over there looks like...
Are you alright?
...Why are you asking?
Because this domain is becoming more and more warped?
Some memory fragments... Not a good sign.
That was quite the...
..."extraordinary Forte," yes?
{PlayerName}, can you step a little to the side?
Hmm?
Like this?
Perhaps a step forward?
Hmm... Maybe a step back?
Alright, this is the last one. Let's see that {Male=handsome;Female=beautiful} smile.
Haha.
(Take a step forward)
(Smile)
(Take another step forward)
This really is an extraordinary Forte.
Shame the New Fed doesn't usually use words like "extraordinary" to describe Fortes...
Oh? It seems we've stumbled upon a little bonus.
A little coaching and you're already a pro.
(I have the photo. Now, where is the right spot to project it?)
Any idea how we find our way out of here?
With our eyes open. The <ano=Photo>key</ano> should be somewhere here.
Excellent. You're catching on quickly.

During your pursuit of the exhibits with Lucilla, a mysterious girl suddenly appears. While you and Lucilla are left briefly dazed, she teleports you both to another research facility. Lucilla, however, seems very familiar with the place.
You reunite with Lucilla within one of her memories, and unexpectedly learn that she had been hiding something from you: apparently, the New Federation has already offered a secret deal with her.

You eventually glimpse the source of Lucilla's inner conflict. In her early years, she approved an experiment that allowed a student to chase a dream, only for it to result in that student's death. This still leaves her deeply burdened with guilt.
You hand Lucilla the prototype entrusted to you by the mysterious girl. Feeling the sincerity behind it, Lucilla finds the courage to face the truth.
Lucilla enters the depths of her memories, and the students within finally speak their hearts to her.
Are you free tomorrow?
I'll take that as a yes. My office, tomorrow morning at 8:00. It's right next to the Academic Affairs Office. Don't mix them up!
What's this about?
I don't see anyone. Are they still on the way?
Hold on, Dr. Luuk says the auditor insisted on driving his own motorbike. That means they're on the second floor. Come on.
Uh, what's all this?
Professor! We heard a very important visitor is coming to tour the Academy. Don't worry, we'll make a good impression!
Yep, we even threw together a little welcoming thing.
Oh, you rascals... Alright, but follow my lead. If this auditor is a by-the-book type, then we—
Aha! WOOO!
Oh yeah! What a ride! Now that was top-notch!
So not a confidential audit, huh?
Welcome to Startorch Academy. I'm Lucilla, the Academy President. So glad you could make it.
WELCOME TO STARTORCH ACADEMY!
Oh! Uh, right. I'm Aalto. Haha... You guys really know how to roll out the red carpet.
Nice to meet you, honored sir! I'm Sigrika, from the Preparatory Program. Thank you for coming to tour the Academy!
Hello, hello! And please, just Aalto is fine. No need for that "honored sir" stuff...
Got it. I'm a Roya, you know! And I just want to say the Academy has been so wonderful to my people. We're all working together to make the world a better place!
Oh! And there are lots of Roya students in Rabelle College too! Everyone works so hard!
Uh? Huh...
Chief Aalto! I'm Dorian from the Agronomy Wing! I've brought you a  Complete Nutrition Squeezy Jelly and our department's special self-heating Cup Noodles!
Cup Noodles? Uh, thanks. And hey, just call me Aalto...
Director Aalto! I'm Misha from the Department of Exostrider Engineering! I couldn't bring my project here, so I'm here to sing instead!
Director, I'm from the Department of Voidmatters, sir! I can dance!
And I can do some custom mods on your bike!
Mr. Aalto.
This is {PlayerName} from Rabelle College. {Male=He;Female=She} will be joining us for the duration of your tour.
What's cooking, Director Aalto?
It's an honor, Esteemed Auditor, sir.
{PlayerName}! What a fantastic name! Not too long, not too short!
Are we supposed to know each other or not?
We are. But don't make it too obvious.
Copy that.
Well then, without further ado, let's head over to Rabelle College. I'll fill you in on our facilities along the way.
That'll be great.
Tell those kids to go their separate ways. I'll meet you at Rabelle College.
Got it.
So... S-so many people?
Someone want to tell me what's happening?
You didn't know, {PlayerName}? Everyone's saying the board is looking to shut down Rabelle College.
No, not the college. Just the Synchronists. A professor covering our Royan History class told us the Spacetrek Collective wants them out of the Academy!
Yeah, well, the rumor mill says Rabelle eats up two-thirds of the Academy's budget, and the Collective's investors have strong opinions 'bout that.
I say investors, but it's mostly New Federation money. Can't say I'm surprised they're pulling this kinda stunt.
What about you, Chisa? What have you heard?
Me? Actually, I don't know the specifics of what's happening. I just wanted to help...
(So it's all just hearsay for now...)
Is this all happening because the Exostrider left?
Why didn't any of the Synchronists show up?
I see. Thanks for filling me in.
Probably. I mean, they were literally picked just to pilot the Exostrider.
But Synchronists are all such brilliant students! Even if they can't pilot anymore, they still...
The New Fed only cares as long as you're an asset. The second you're not, you're out.
(There must be more to it than that.)
That's what's strange to me. But Professor Lucilla only had {PlayerName} come, so maybe it's not as serious as we think?
Why do I feel like asking Senior to come means the opposite?
That Aalto guy... he's got a reputation in New Fed's circles. Known for handling intel, if you catch my drift.
Isn't this supposed to be a cooperative visit...? Why's the Black Shores sending his type here?
(I'd better check the situation at Rabelle College.)
The President and I are on it. You guys should head back for now.
Hm, well... Gimme a shout if you need backup! There's no way I'm letting them do the Synchronists dirty like this!
We're counting on you, Senior!
We trust you!
(Head over now.)
(Head over later.)
In addition to Augmented Resonance training, we place strong emphasis on general education for our Synchronists. This is Professor Mornye who teaches Synth Armament Studies.
Shall we sit in for a bit, Mr. Aalto? Before we tour the student projects?
If it's no trouble?
Alright. In the last lecture, we proved that the Ruehl Equation holds true for Type-II Synth Armaments. Today, we'll move on to their Tuning Stability Constants.
Lixian, could you please write the final derivation from the last lecture on the board?
Yes... Professor..
While she gets started, let's do a quick review. Waleo, what is the standard medium used to measure Tuning Stability in a lab setting?
It's s-so... s-so... mmm...
Yes, sodium. An interesting choice, though its volatility makes it impractical for standard testing.
Sonia, could you tell me the standard medium for determining Tuning Stability in Synth Armaments under laboratory conditions?
Mm... S-squ... Squeezy... Jelly...
Squeezy Jelly, you say... Well, it seems we moved through the material a bit too quickly last time.
But that's alright. Everyone, please refocus. Let's go over Lixian's board work—
As you can see, Mr. Aalto, this is our signature "Sleep Learning Program."
Oooh! Very impressive! Ahem... How about we move on to the next stop?
After you.
Hang in there.
I'll see you later.
Now we're about to show you some Augmented Resonance projects developed by our Synchronists.
Among them, the unmanned vehicle prototype shows exceptional promise across multiple market sectors—
Absent Students: 8. Data uploaded to cloud storage.
These children... seem to have forgotten the importance of honoring their commitments.
(What's the deal?)
(Looks like the students all skipped class.)
Ahaha! Maybe we're just too early, President Lucilla. Why don't we take a stroll elsewhere? I'm actually quite curious about the Academy's catering system!
Hah... My apologies, Mr. Aalto. How fortunate we are to have you here despite our apparent lack of preparation.
There's no point denying it. You're seeing firsthand how the ongoing debate within the Spacetrek Collective has begun to affect our students.
Startorch needs support now more than ever.
(Shoot a knowing look toward Aalto.)
(Stay silent.)
(Got any solutions?)
(Not really...)
(Dragging the Black Shores into this might make things difficult for Shorekeeper. Let's just observe for now.)
I understand, President. And this is precisely why I'm here to convey the—
Mr. Aalto, how about we add an extra tour this evening? We can discuss anything you'd like after that.
Uh... Works for me?
{PlayerName}, I'll take Mr. Aalto for a meal, then. Would you mind checking back in with Professor Mornye for me?
(See—You—On—WavesLine.)
Why didn't you wake them up?
This class is difficult to follow, so it's normal for some to drift off. Still, it's rare for the entire class to go like that.
If only I could make my lectures more accessible...
This isn't your fault.
It's like metal fatigue. These students are being tempered and pushed to their limits over and over. Eventually, the metal just snaps.
Should I have woken them? Reprimanded them? Or offered them assurance...?
I've heard about the pressure they've been under lately. Maybe the best thing is a few days away from all this...
Don't worry. Lucilla and I will take care of it.
Thank you, Mentor.
Be at the square by 8. The one we passed earlier. Got some intel to share.
OK.
Any recs on what to order? Lucilla went back to her office to take care of something.
Just order everything on the menu.
Get the cheap ones so you can toss them without feeling guilty.
Gotcha!
That bad? Now I HAVE to try 'em!
OK.
Just order everything on the menu.
Get the cheap ones so you can toss them without feeling guilty.
You have my deepest respect. Working in this food desert takes a special kind of fortitude.
What did you have for dinner?
Why is Encore not with you?
Tell me what happened.
Something that looked like toothpaste. Didn't go down well. Next thing I know, there were students everywhere shoving snacks at me like it was my birthday.
Ugh, hellish.
I couldn't convince her. She hit me with "I'm too grown up for school now."
But that's fine. I asked President Lucilla to give me some "grown-up" worksheets. See how she likes those, hmph!

To put it simply? The Exostrider's gone, so the Synchronist Program needs to go. Problem is, everyone has a different idea of what to do with those students—And by "everyone," I mean President Lucilla versus everyone else.
Anyway, the New Federation and the majority of the board want to pull the plug immediately and draft a new teaching plan from scratch.

Meanwhile, the Executive Committee moderates have promised to stay out of it, as long as their nation's Synchronists are covered. With either guaranteed support back home or a smooth transfer somewhere else.
Where does Lucilla stand?
She wants to continue the Synchronist Program.
Continue?
Yep. Confusing, isn't it? Speaking of which... how well do you know her, {PlayerName}?
Pretty well.
(Do I really know her, though?)
Hm. I see.
Hm, so you're not so sure either, huh?
I'll be honest with you, {PlayerName}. The Black Shores doesn't trust her right now.
Between her proposal, her deep New Fed connections, and that evasive attitude... There are just too many uncertainties for us to take on the risk of helping her.
At least, that's the conclusion we've reached based on the facts we have so far.
But... the Bloombearers who graduated from Startorch heard about this and stepped up to endorse Lucilla. That's what changed Shorekeeper's mind.
A teacher who gets that kind of trust from her students... That's pretty impressive.
So what do you need from me?
Actually, according to Shorekeeper, you are the one really running this audit.
So we need you, acting as both a Startorch student and a Black Shores auditor, to tell us if Lucilla is solid. And what she's really planning.
(I want to do something for the Synchronists, but I've also got my responsibility to the Black Shores. I don't think Lucilla would put her students in harm's way, but still...)
Got it. I'll do what I can to help you.
I should be the one saying that to you. Anyway, we need a plan for—
Great, another grand plan. Why'd you gotta make everything so complicated?
What the—?! How's that—?!
Helloooo, Mr. Aalto! This is a once-in-a-lifetime chance to invest in the Exostrider Project. I suggest the Black Shores chips in... this much!
Or, you can just patch me through to the Collective's board. I'd be happy to handle the negotiations myself!
Is this... Aemeath? I can't believe she just hacked a Black Shores Terminal!
Aemeath...
This is serious...
Ahem! I am being serious! If Synchronist degrees get canceled, my record will say I only finished Roya preschool!
Besides, keeping Rabelle College around isn't that hard. Get creative. Talk to Chase. Talk to Shorekeeper. The Collective's investors can't be tougher to handle than Aleph-1, right?
So what if they don't care about your contributions? If they actually want you on their side, they'll have to listen anyway. That's how leverage works.
(Aemeath might actually be a genius.)
(No, that's too reckless.)
If we lean on that kind of leverage now, we'll be held to it later. My experience has shown me that it's often better to act as an individual.
Since you're planning on the "savior" career path, I think you'll understand what I mean, Aemeath.
Hmm, makes sense. Kinda old-school thinking, though.
(I need to figure out what Lucilla is really thinking. Then I'll play it by ear.)
If I want them to protect the Synchronists when I can't, I've got to work inside their system. That's just how this game works.
Trust me and Lucilla. We'll find the right way to handle this.
Ha! Alright then. But just so you know, if my school record disappears, I'm renaming the Spacetrek Collective to the "Aemeath Collective!"
Honestly? If we let Aemeath loose on them, it might actually take some pressure off Lucilla.
But like she said, she's a Synchronist too. That just makes her one more person Lucilla has to protect.
Fair enough. But I'm afraid we have less time than we thought.
I spotted some New Fed spies back at the station. Lost 'em on the motorbike, but it won't be long before they track us here.
Before Lucilla's next tour begins, let's poke around and see what we can find.
Students run flea markets on campus? I'm starting to get the hype!
Wait, isn't that the student who dozed off in class earlier? C'mon, let's go over.
If we follow this method, the convergence radius for this series is obviously—
Y-yes, I'm following! Mm-hmm!
...I'm terrible at explaining this, aren't I?
No, no! I'm just slow! I-I'll focus harder!
No. You paid me to tutor you, and I'll make sure you get your money's worth!
Here, I'll write down a third way to solve it. Watch how it goes, okay?
Okay!
(So that's why she was drowsy in class... She's been staying up late tutoring other students.)
You're telling me you've modified every bike here? That's insane.
Well, Waleo's been in the expedition motorbike program since day one. These bikes here are basically his family!
Soulmates.
So, whaddya say, Auditor Aalto? How about you order ten as a starter pack!
(Ten soulmates sold in a pack, huh...)
I heard you test-drove the Academy's stock model this morning. With the rain the last two days, probably felt a little slip on the turns, yeah?
Try this one. I tweaked the ABS and TCS myself. You could take this straight to a pro race, no problem.
No wonder you were sleeping in class. Up all night in the garage?
No. Bikes have been ready for weeks. Last night, I was just... saying goodbye to them.
(Well, that's depressing. I'd feel bad buying them now.)
Not a problem. For project funding approvals, we can follow the New Federation model.
But when it comes to picking research topics, I'm afraid I must insist on giving our teams more freedom to choose their own direction.
(Lucilla's busy now. I should wait outside.)
Hands off, you little—
Never!
...Please don't fight, you two. Um, maybe I'll just check out the other stalls...
Don't go, Chisa! You've got a real eye for quality. This piece was meant for you!
